rounds.text: Spunweb Nonwoven Ltd exhibits severe cash flow constraints, as evidenced by a dismal cash conversion rate of 0.13x for March 2026, indicating that reported profits are far ahead of actual cash generation [E23]. This cash deficit is driven by working capital days increasing from 41.7 days to 77.9 days [E43], which restricted March 2026 operating cash flow to just Rs 3 Cr [E24]—representing only 23% of operating profit [E26]—and resulted in a deeply negative free cash flow of Rs -31 Cr [E25]. Reflecting these underlying balance sheet pressures, institutional investors are exiting, with negative institutional money flow [E34] driven by drops in both foreign [E32] and domestic [E33] institutional holdings, while the stock price has fallen -26% over the past year [E16]. Furthermore, despite reporting profits, the company pays no dividend [E4] [E42], and it remains exposed to input cost volatility as market uncertainty continues to cause polypropylene price hikes [E64]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong historical growth, including a 43% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E13], a 114% compounded profit growth over the same period [E15], and a high return on equity of 27.4% [E11]. Yet, because these earnings are not translating into cash [E23], the stock remains depressed at just 20% of the way up its 52-week range [E5].
